producer_report.summary: Root cause: neither the reader's brief nor the planner's brief told the stage to read a reused struct field, CLI argument, record key or config key for its documented meaning. Jobs 20261030-013421-tfwf and 20261113-194336-scfc each matched a field by name. The fix is information, not a refusal. READING_RULES in reader.rs gains one generic `(prose only)` line requiring a `Field meaning:` assumption. It must quote the documented meaning with a path:line, say why it fits and, for a config key, give the live athena.toml value, or else plan a new field. planner.rs gains `FIELD_MEANING_RULE`, printed in the planner brief's Report, with the same instruction. No crates/athena-core file changes, so the expected share of past accepted readings newly refused is 0%. In the `mod tests` of briefs.rs I moved the pins the new text moves (the rule count to 13, the section bounds, the Report bound) and added two tests on the rendered briefs. CHANGELOG.md gets an entry and docs/decisions.md gets D180. The prompt files are untouched. The full `cargo test --locked` finished with exit code 0 in the background.

checks_run.note: 142 passed, including the two new tests and the moved pins
Moved to the background after the foreground limit; the completion notice reported exit code 0. I could not read its output.

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-context (run `cargo test -p athena-context`) renders the reader brief and asserts its Reading rules section contains a rule requiring, for each reused existing struct field, CLI argument, record key or config key, a `Field meaning:` assumption quoting the documented meaning with a crates/ path:line and why it matches, or a new field when it does not. The test fails on the code before the change.
criteria_check.evidence: The new test `the_reader_brief_requires_a_field_meaning_assumption_for_a_reused_field` in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs renders reader_brief and finds the rendered bullet containing `Field meaning:`. It asserts the phrases CLI argument, record key, config key, documented meaning, crates/, path:line, why it fits, live athena.toml value, new field and quote. It passes in `cargo test -p athena-context` (142 passed). Before the change no READING_RULES line contains `Field meaning:`, so the `.expect` in the test fails. I did not run the test against the old code.

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-context (`cargo test -p athena-context`) asserts the planner prompt/brief carries the same instruction, so a plan that reuses a field must quote its documented meaning and check the live athena.toml value; it fails before the change.
criteria_check.evidence: The new test `the_planner_brief_requires_a_reused_field_to_quote_its_meaning_and_check_the_live_config` renders planner_brief. It asserts FIELD_MEANING_RULE appears exactly once in the Report, after REAL_RECORDS_RULE, with the phrases struct field, CLI argument, record key, config key, documented meaning, crates/, path:line, live athena.toml value, each role and new field. It passes. Before the change the constant does not exist, so the test does not compile.

criteria_check.criterion: The new rule is generic (any field, CLI argument, record key or config key), not specific to restart `via` or `hard_producer_*`; the diff of crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs shows it added to the Reading rules list marked `(prose only)`.
criteria_check.evidence: The reader.rs diff changes the array type from [&str; 12] to [&str; 13] and adds one element ending `(prose only).`. The extended test `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` asserts the line has no token `via`, no `restart`, `hard_producer` or `check_`, and ends with `(prose only).`. It passes.

criteria_check.criterion: The diff adds no new refusing check in crates/athena-core; the information is given in the brief and prompt, so expected 0% of past accepted readings are newly refused.
criteria_check.evidence: `git status --short` lists only CHANGELOG.md, crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs, crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs and docs/decisions.md. No crates/athena-core path is in it, and the new reader line carries no check name.

criteria_check.criterion: The CHANGELOG.md entry names the root cause (the reading and plan stages were never told to verify a reused field's documented meaning) and cites jobs 20261030-013421-tfwf and 20261113-194336-scfc; any decision is recorded as a new appended docs/decisions.md entry with a Provenance bullet.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md gains an entry at the top of [Unreleased] / Added. It names the root cause that neither stage was ever told to verify a reused field's documented meaning, and it cites both jobs. docs/decisions.md gains D180 after D179, with a Provenance bullet and no edit to an existing line. `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` (4 passed) and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` (22 passed) both pass.

open_issues: crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs is not a listed deliverable. I edited only its `mod tests`, because its pins on the rule count and section sizes fail on the new text, as the plan said.
learnings: The Bash hook allows only cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm for the producer. grep, tail, sed and echo are refused, and paths outside the working directory cannot be read or redirected to.
The full `cargo test --locked` takes more than 20 minutes in this environment.
The reader and planner brief size pins and fixtures are private to `mod tests` in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs.
desires: A way to read output from a background run, and a command that stays within the foreground time limit.
